learning_outcomes.text: To provide students knowledge in the field of expert/knowledge systems and rule-based programming.

syllabus_topics: The principles and architecture of expert/knowledge systems
Examples from the field of artificial intelligence
Introduction to fuzzy mathematics and inference
assessment_rules: The examination is in written and oral form, consisting of two programming tasks and one theoretical question. The approximate evaluation scale is A 90%, B 80%, C 70%, D 60%, E 50%. The scale of assessment (preliminary/final) is 0/100.
bibliography: Giarratano, Joseph C., and Gary D. Riley. Expert systems: principles and programming. Brooks/Cole Publishing Co., 2005.
Tadeusiewicz, Ryszard. "Introduction to intelligent systems." Intelligent systems. CRC Press, 2018.
Smith, Suzanne, and Abraham Kandel. Verification and validation of rule-based expert systems. CRC Press, 2018.
Krishnamoorthy, C. S., and S. Rajeev. Artificial Intelligence and Expert Systems for Artificial Intelligence Engineers. CRC press, 2018.
institution: Univerzita Komenského v Bratislave (Comenius University Bratislava)
degree: Bachelor Applied Informatics (1-AIN), Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Informatics
